title: Player archetype clustering (UMAP + HDBSCAN), per season
author: andrew
rationale: Discover coarse and fine-grained player archetypes from season-aggregate stats, per season, unsupervised.
question: Do FPL players fall into interpretable coarse/fine archetypes from season-aggregate production stats, consistently across seasons?
method_summary: Per season, players >=900 min; 23 production/rate features (no minutes); UMAP(10D)->HDBSCAN(leaf) for fine; agglomerate fine centroids to K=5 for coarse (nested). Seed 42.
key_findings: 5 stable coarse archetypes/season: GK, elite attackers, creative mids, attacking full-backs, defensive/rotation defenders.
Fine gives 7-9 nested sub-roles (goalscorer vs playmaker; attacking vs defensive full-back).
Position is recovered without being a feature - archetypes are football-sensible.
A minutes floor (>=900) is essential; otherwise coarse clustering just recovers played-vs-not-played.
Coarse via merging fine centroids is stable across seasons; a 2nd independent HDBSCAN was not.
